author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader opens a specialty directory listing every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each followed by the veterinarians holding it by first and last name. All specialties show at once, with no paging. A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the directory is opened, then every one of them is listed under the name it is stored by.
Given a specialty that veterinarians hold, when the directory is opened, then each of those veterinarians is listed under it by first name then last name.
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on the page.
Given the clinic's specialties, when the directory is opened, then all of them are shown at once and nothing is offered to page through.
Given the directory, when it is opened, then it offers no way to add, rename, or remove a specialty, and none to change who holds one.
Given any page of the system, when it is rendered, then nothing on it leads to the specialty directory.
Given the supported languages, when the directory's wording is checked, then every piece of it is present in each of them.
Edge case 1: a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it.
Edge case 2: a veterinarian holding more than one specialty is listed under each of them.
Edge case 3: the specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one.
Edge case 4: when the clinic knows no specialty at all, the page is shown with nothing listed rather than failing.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application — NG-2 stands unchanged
A navigation entry for the directory, or a link to it from any other page — the owner defers a visible entry point to a possible follow-up request
notes: Owner-stated address for the page: GET /specialties.html — recorded here rather than in the PRD, which names no route; the design stage owns placing it in system-design.md#contracts. REQ-SYS-001 still binds the new page, so it carries the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory; what REQ-SPC-001 forbids is a link in the other direction. Three open product questions were recorded in the PRD's Open Questions rather than consulted, per the dispatch: whether the directory gets a visible entry point, what order the entries take (a stable order is the bar), and whether a specialty no veterinarian holds should be marked as unheld. file_targets are best-effort: the controller and template may end up new files rather than the vet ones listed.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fresh ground: nothing in durable memory records a specialty-major read path. The vet feature package owns both Vet and Specialty, so the slice stays inside it and adds no package and no cross-package edge. Three gaps make it more than an adjustment. (1) No repository reads Specialty, and VetRepository cannot supply a specialty no veterinarian holds (edge case 1). (2) The persisted association runs Vet to Specialty only, so the specialty-major shape must be built rather than queried. (3) The page is a second HTTP surface, not a variant of /vets.html. Recorded in system-design.md#contracts as three designed rows plus an invariants paragraph, and in ADR 2026-08-11-specialty-major-view-by-association-inversion.md. Basis for the covering-code claims is grep over the vet package and templates, plus reading VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Specialty, CacheConfiguration, fragments/layout.html and vets/vetList.html in full; the IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker basis.
integration_points: New HTTP surface GET /specialties.html served by a package-private SpecialtyController in the vet package; the owner-stated address is now recorded in system-design.md#contracts
New SpecialtyRepository extending Spring Data Repository over Specialty, reading the whole set; PetTypeRepository is the precedent for a lookup-entity repository in a feature package
VetRepository.findAll() is reused unchanged as the veterinarian side; it is @Cacheable("vets") and Vet fetches its specialties EAGER, so one call supplies both sides
New SpecialtyDirectory value object pairs each specialty with its holders and fixes the order; it is the unit under test for every ordering and grouping criterion
Template joins fragments/layout.html with a menu argument matching no existing menuItem, so the page carries the standard navigation (REQ-SYS-001) with no entry highlighted
No menuItem is added to fragments/layout.html and no th:href to the new route is added anywhere, satisfying the acceptance criterion that nothing leads to the directory

patterns.description: Value object (In force): SpecialtyDirectory is immutable, equal by value, has no identity, and is not framework-instantiated, so the persistence-entity exception does not apply to it
Repository over a lookup entity inside its feature package, returning results in name order; the SpecialtyRepository precedent
Read-only GET mapping ending in .html, resolving a view under templates/<feature>/; SpecialtyController follows this shape
Layout fragment usage with the active-menu argument; the new template passes a value matching no menuItem

risks.risk: Grouping veterinarians under specialties inside SpecialtyController would be a fresh Web-controller violation; architecture-principles.md states the existing controller deviation does not extend to new rules
risks.mitigation: The inversion and the ordering live in SpecialtyDirectory, unit-testable with real Vet and Specialty instances and no Spring context; the controller reads both repositories, calls the factory, and selects the view

risks.risk: Annotating the specialty read @Cacheable with a new cache name fails at runtime; CacheConfiguration creates only the "vets" cache and the JCache manager does not create caches on demand
risks.mitigation: Leave the specialty read uncached this slice; a second uninvalidated cache would also compound Open Question 5

risks.risk: Delegating the sort to the database repeats the PostgreSQL collation divergence already recorded under Known Defects, making the stable-order criterion vendor-dependent
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory sorts in Java with an explicit comparator: specialty by name, veterinarians by last then first name; the ADR records the divergence from PetTypeRepository

risks.risk: Adding new message keys multiplies across eleven bundles and the I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build on any gap or on literal text in the template
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys first: specialties, vets, name. Every new key lands in all eleven files in the same commit; no literal text in the template

risks.risk: Being unlinked is obscurity, not access control; the page is reachable by anyone who knows the address, as every route in this application is
risks.mitigation: The page discloses nothing that /vets.html does not already publish, and it takes no request parameter at all, so the slice adds no trust boundary and no new input to validate

risks.risk: The whole specialty and veterinarian sets are paired in memory with no paging, by requirement
risks.mitigation: Both are lookup-scale here; the ADR records that a large roster needs a different read path

notes: file_targets in the prd-entry are superseded, as that record itself anticipated: the controller, repository, read model, template and tests are new files in the vet package and templates/specialties/, and VetController, VetRepository and vets/vetList.html are untouched. The prd-entry's seven test_names still stand verbatim; the four that are pure grouping and ordering assertions belong on SpecialtyDirectoryTests, the rest on SpecialtyControllerTests with MockMvc. An eighth test is needed for the criterion that no page leads to the directory. Residual open question, recorded rather than consulted per the dispatch: the PRD asks whether a specialty no veterinarian holds should be marked as unheld. The narrowest reading is taken here, so such a specialty is listed with nothing under it and the existing 'none' key is not reused to label it; a later product answer would change only the template. The other two PRD open questions, a visible entry point and the exact order, are settled for this slice by the owner's decisions and by the Java-side comparator respectively. Not in scope and not mine: scripts/layout.toml declares spec_version 0.1.0 against manifest 0.2.0, a pre-existing harness-install mismatch outside docs/ and outside this slice. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectory is a well-documented immutable read model: private constructor, static factory `of`, final class, javadoc explains the why (inverted association, Java-side ordering, identity-based pairing) rather than restating the what

The BY_VETERINARIAN_NAME comparator's explicit `(Vet veterinarian) -> veterinarian.getLastName()` lambda instead of a `Person::getLastName` method reference is not a style regression: verified by compiling both forms — the method-reference chain fails javac type inference (Comparator<Person> is not assignable to Comparator<Vet>) while the explicit-parameter lambda fixes the target type; the current code is the necessary form

Pairing by persisted id (not reference or name) is judged sound: VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable("vets") while SpecialtyRepository's read is uncached, so the same row arrives as two distinct instances and reference-equality pairing would silently yield no holders; Specialty.name carries an index but no uniqueness constraint (checked db/h2/schema.sql), so name-based pairing risks merging distinct rows. The one-line javadoc on `holds()` states this rationale in the code itself, not only the ADR

SpecialtyDirectory declaring no equals/hashCode is judged sound and properly bounded: its contents are persisted JPA entities with identity-only equality, so a field-wise equals would present a value-equality contract the type cannot honor; the divergence from the architecture-principles Value-object row is stated in both the class javadoc and the ADR's Consequences section, scoped to this one type only

SpecialtyController and SpecialtyRepository mirror the established VetController/VetRepository and PetTypeRepository precedents (package-private controller, constructor injection, <code> javadoc tag style, GET-only mapping resolving templates/<feature>/) with no unjustified deviation
checkFormat passes clean on the change set; no checkstyle or format issues in the four new production files or the template

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No new attack surface class: GET /specialties.html takes no path variable, query parameter, request body, or @ModelAttribute, so there is no request-derived value anywhere in the new code. Nothing to validate at the boundary because nothing crosses it.

Data access is a Spring Data derived findAll() on SpecialtyRepository plus the existing cached VetRepository.findAll(). No @Query, no createQuery, no string-concatenated query text. The injection-into-data-access row of security-principles.md passes.

Output escaping is intact. specialtyList.html renders every dynamic value through th:text (entry.specialty.name, veterinarian.firstName/lastName) with Thymeleaf default escaping on. Swept the template for the whole XSS class: no th:utext, no [( )] unescaped inlining, no th:inline, no th:onclick/th:href/th:src, no script block. Stored specialty and veterinarian names therefore cannot break out as markup.

Exposure judgment: the new unauthenticated route publishes veterinarian full names and specialty names, which the baseline already publishes unauthenticated at /vets.html and, unpaged and in full, at the /vets @ResponseBody route. The change discloses no data class not already reachable at the same trust level and adds no PII beyond it, so it does not leave the application weaker than the Security Context baseline in system-design.md. The exposure is stated in the PRD and in system-design.md #contracts, satisfying the 'a change that adds an endpoint states what it exposes and to whom' row.

Unbounded render judged and cleared as a security matter: the whole specialty set plus the vet set render on one page by product decision, and the pairing is an in-memory nested scan. The vet side is served from the declared cache; only the specialty read reaches the database per request, over a lookup-scale table. The pre-existing /vets route already performs an unpaged full-collection read, so this is not a new class and not a regression against baseline. Recorded as an accepted characteristic, not a finding; the ADR already names the large-roster case as needing a different read path.

No new endpoint mutates state and none accepts serialized input. The controller returns a fixed view name (no request-derived view or resource path, so no path-traversal or template-injection vector) and carries no @ResponseBody, so no content-negotiated representation is added. Mass-assignment and identifier-tampering rows do not apply: no request-bound type is introduced, hence no @InitBinder disallow list is owed.

No secret material introduced. Swept the three new Java files, the template, and the three test classes for password/secret/token/key/credential names: no hits. No new logging and no new exception message, so nothing new can reach the error page that renders exception text.

Supply chain clean: the change set touches no build.gradle, pom.xml, gradle wrapper, or settings file, and adds no dependency. dependencyCheckAnalyze and a dependencies diff would report against an unchanged graph, so neither was run.

The unlinked address is correctly framed as a product decision in the PRD and ADR, not claimed anywhere as a security control, so nothing in the docs teaches a reader that reachability-by-address-only protects the page.

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: All seven test_names from the prd-entry are present and pass: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByItsStoredName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEachHoldingVeterinarianByFirstThenLastName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitAVeterinarianHoldingNoSpecialty, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowEverySpecialtyAtOnceWithoutPaging, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListAVeterinarianUnderEachSpecialtyTheyHold, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderEmptyWhenTheClinicKnowsNoSpecialty. The design's eighth test, noPageShouldLinkToTheSpecialtyDirectory, covers the negative-link acceptance criterion. jacoco confirms 100% instruction coverage on SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyDirectory.Entry, and SpecialtyController, well past the brief's 80% domain-package target

Verified the implementer's claim in design-block line 8: every Specialty and Vet fixture in SpecialtyDirectoryTests (specialty() and vet() factories) and SpecialtyControllerTests explicitly calls setId() with distinct integers (1,2,3), so holds()'s Objects.equals(id,id) pairing is genuinely exercised in theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian rather than vacuously true from two null ids -- claim confirmed against the actual test code, not just the design narrative

SpecialtyDirectoryLinkAbsenceTests is a sound pin for the negative criterion for this codebase: cross-checked fragments/layout.html and vetList.html and every th:href in this app's templates is a literal path string ('/vets.html', '/owners/find', etc.), not a computed/variable expression, so the literal-substring sweep across every *.html under templates/ cannot be evaded by a link this codebase's own conventions would produce; Files.walk plus the isNotEmpty() guard also protects against a silently-empty template set masking a false pass

Edge cases from the prd-entry are all covered with real, distinguishable fixtures rather than invented or degenerate data: edge case 1 (specialty held by no vet) and edge case 2 (vet holding two specialties, listed under each) both use named AssertJ satisfiesExactly/singleElement chains, not loops or branching; edge case 4 (empty clinic) is covered at the controller layer via hasProperty("entries", empty())

Mocking stays within the brief's policy: SpecialtyDirectoryTests uses only real Specialty/Vet value objects with zero mocks; SpecialtyControllerTests uses @WebMvcTest+MockMvc (the one sanctioned mock, standing in for HTTP transport) with @MockitoBean repositories, mirroring the existing VetControllerTests precedent for the same layer boundary

AssertJ used throughout with no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue; three-tier data naming is respected (DENTISTRY/RADIOLOGY/SURGERY named by role, vet()/specialty() factories keep construction out of raw `new`); four-phase structure held with blank-line separation and no phase-comment narration; test names follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school

I18n acceptance criterion (AC7) needs no new test: SpecialtyController and specialtyList.html use only pre-existing message keys (specialties, name, vets), verified present in all eleven locale bundles under src/main/resources/messages/, so the existing I18nPropertiesSyncTest already covers it without modification

blast_radius.note: Eleven files but nothing existing is edited outside docs: all four production files and all three test files are new, confined to the vet feature package plus one new template directory. No schema, build, config, message-bundle, or layout-fragment change, no sensitive path, and the new GET /specialties.html route collides with nothing. The only shared surfaces touched are three documentation files.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do what their size and description promise. I checked the traps this shape invites and each is clean: vets arrive from a cached repository but Vet maps specialties EAGER, so getSpecialties() on detached instances cannot throw; pairing goes through persisted id rather than reference or name, which is the correct choice given the cached-versus-uncached read; the template renders every dynamic value through escaping th:text with no unescaped inlining; the layout is invoked with a menu name matching no existing entry, so no navigation link appears; and the three message keys the page uses already exist in the default bundle and in every non-empty locale bundle, so REQ-LANG-002 holds without new keys. Two residuals, both deliberate and disclosed in the ADR: two unsaved entities would pair with each other since Objects.equals of two nulls is true, unreachable from repository reads; and veterinarians sort by last name while rendering first-then-last.

test_adequacy.note: Eight tests that would fail against a broken implementation rather than restate it. The ordering test feeds an unordered list and asserts an exact sorted sequence; the per-specialty test feeds veterinarians in reverse and asserts the corrected order, so it pins the comparator rather than input order; the omission test asserts exactly the holding veterinarian; the empty-clinic case asserts empty entries. The link-absence test walks every template for the literal route with a non-empty guard against a vacuous pass. Directory tests use real Specialty and Vet objects with no mocks; only the repository seams at the controller are stubbed. Minor gaps: no two-veterinarians-same-last-name case exercising the first-name tiebreak, and the no-paging assertion is a proxy on absent page markup.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four latest verdicts are approved with empty findings lists. The first round carried one doc changes_requested holding an autofix and one clarify tagged with a consistent-with-codebase bar clause about a literal route in the contracts table; it was resolved on the merits by moving the address into the Constants table, and the doc reviewer's second approval endorses that reasoning specifically rather than merely accepting it. Security and test reviewers are silent in the fix round because the risk-proportional plan scoped a docs-only fix delta, which the code-quality reviewer independently verified by diffing trees; that silence is expected, not a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries and zero consultations. The one design revision was the recorded design-mismatch abort, which the record itself diagnoses as a bookkeeping gap in the design block's declared doc paths with no code defect, and the superseding block closed it. Reading the diff against the requirement, every file serves the stated surface: the page, its read model, its repository, its tests, the PRD entry, the ADR, and the design rows. The only edit reaching past the slice is a general provenance convention in system-design.md for marking designed-but-unlanded statements, which is small and was doc-reviewed.

rationale: A self-contained additive feature: new files only, no existing production code touched, escaped output, no request-derived input, and tests that pin ordering and filtering rather than restate them. The eager-fetch and identity-pairing traps I checked are all handled. Confirm and merge.
